categories.main_business_segments: Brown & Brown, Inc. operates through four primary business segments: Retail, National Programs, Wholesale Brokerage, and Services. The Retail segment provides a broad range of insurance products and services to commercial, public, professional, and individual customers, as well as non-insurance warranty services. The National Programs segment acts as a managing general agent (MGA), offering specialized insurance programs for niche markets. The Wholesale Brokerage segment markets and sells excess and surplus insurance products primarily through independent agents and brokers. The Services segment provides insurance-related services such as third-party claims administration and medical utilization management.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary technology platforms and data analytics to support insurance placement, risk management, and claims administration. It operates as an intermediary, primarily using digital tools for policy management, customer engagement, and integration of acquired businesses. Brown & Brown also utilizes specialized underwriting and claims management systems, particularly in its MGA and TPA (third-party administrator) operations, and participates in capitalized captive insurance facilities to provide additional underwriting capacity.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Brown & Brown serves a diverse customer base including commercial businesses, public and quasi-public entities, professionals, individuals, affinity groups, and insurance carriers. Key end markets include property and casualty, employee benefits, personal insurance, specialty programs for specific industries, and insurance-related services for self-insured entities and government programs. No single customer accounts for a material portion of revenue, reflecting a broad and diversified client base.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company primarily operates in the United States, with significant concentrations in Florida, California, Massachusetts, Georgia, New York, and Michigan. Internationally, it has operations in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Belgium, Bermuda, Cayman Islands, Canada, and Italy. In 2022, international operations generated approximately $240.6 million in revenue, with the majority of business still concentrated in the U.S.
categories.supply_chain_position: Brown & Brown operates primarily as an intermediary in the insurance supply chain, functioning as an agent, broker, MGA, and TPA. It is positioned downstream, connecting insurance carriers with end customers and providing value-added services such as risk management, claims administration, and program management. The company assumes limited underwriting risk, mainly through its participation in captive insurance facilities and a write-your-own flood insurance carrier.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic priorities include organic growth, targeted acquisitions, technological innovation, and expanding its presence in specialty and international markets. Brown & Brown invests in digital transformation, integration of acquired businesses, and development of proprietary analytics and customer-facing platforms. It emphasizes a decentralized, meritocratic culture to drive performance and innovation, and is focused on enhancing operational efficiency and expanding its product and service offerings.
categories.revenue_model: Brown & Brown generates revenue primarily through commissions paid by insurance carriers, which are typically a percentage of premiums placed, and through fees for services such as claims administration, consulting, and program management. Additional revenue streams include profit-sharing contingent commissions based on underwriting results, fees in lieu of commissions, and, to a lesser extent, retained earned premiums from captive insurance facilities.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include large global insurance brokers such as Marsh & McLennan, Aon, Willis Towers Watson, and Arthur J. Gallagher, as well as regional and specialty firms. Brown & Brown is positioned as one of the largest insurance intermediaries in the U.S., with a focus on decentralized operations, niche program expertise, and a strong acquisition track record. The company competes on innovation, service quality, industry knowledge, and price.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2022, Brown & Brown reported total revenues of $3.57 billion, representing a 17.1% increase over the prior year, with organic revenue growth of 8.1%. Net income was $671.8 million, up 14.4% year-over-year. The company has demonstrated consistent growth through both organic expansion and acquisitions, with a compound annual revenue growth rate of 13.3% since 1993. Total assets at year-end 2022 were $13.97 billion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Brown & Brown differentiates itself through its decentralized, entrepreneurial culture, broad product and service offerings, and expertise in niche and specialty insurance programs. The company emphasizes customer-centric service, innovation, and operational agility, supported by proprietary technology and analytics. Its ability to deliver tailored solutions, deep industry knowledge, and a strong track record of successful acquisitions underpin its value proposition to clients and carrier partners.
